name: System Last Shutdown Time
os_min: Windows XP (ShutdownCount value is Windows XP only)
location: SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Windows (ShutdownTime value) ; SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Watchdog\Display (ShutdownCount value, Windows XP only)
purpose: Records the last time the system was shut down; on Windows XP, also records a running count of the total number of shutdowns.
key_fields: ShutdownTime - 64-bit Windows FILETIME value for the most recent shutdown
ShutdownCount - running shutdown counter (Windows XP only)
normal_baseline: ShutdownTime consistent with routine business-hours shutdown/reboot patterns or a known scheduled-maintenance window for that host.
anomalies: ShutdownTime immediately preceding or following other incident indicators, consistent with an attacker-forced reboot to complete malware/driver installation or to disrupt live-response collection of volatile evidence
ShutdownTime inconsistent with other timeline artifacts for uptime/boot activity, suggesting the value or the system clock was manipulated

A ShutdownTime value present despite other evidence indicating the system was never gracefully shut down (e.g., crash/power-loss indicators), suggesting the value was set through an unexpected process rather than a genuine shutdown
anti_forensic_notes: ShutdownTime is a single value overwritten on every shutdown, so it only ever reflects the MOST RECENT shutdown - no history of prior shutdowns is retained here. Cross-reference System.evtx (e.g., Event ID 1074/6006 style shutdown/service-stop records) for a fuller shutdown/reboot history than this single registry value can provide on its own.
interpretation: Determining the last shutdown time can help detect user behavior and system anomalies. The value is stored in 64-bit Windows FILETIME format.
